# GEDCOM 5.5 and 5.5.1 coverage

What this library does with every structure GEDCOM 5.5 and 5.5.1 define: 1408
distinct (superstructure, tag) pairs across the two versions — 998 in 5.5 and 1316 in 5.5.1 — each
measured against the decoder rather than estimated. The GEDCOM 7.0 half is
[a separate document](gedcom-7-coverage.md), derived the same way.

Coverage is reported per pair, not per tag, because GEDCOM tag meaning depends
on where the tag appears. `RELI` under an individual and `RELI` under an event are
different structures, and this library may well support one and not the other. A
flat per-tag table would overstate support.

The two versions are reported together because they share most of a grammar.
Where they agree, one row says so; where they differ, the row shows it.

## Where the specification comes from

7.0 is published with machine-readable extracted files. 5.5 and 5.5.1 are not:
their structure set exists only as the semi-formal Lineage-Linked Grammar
printed in Chapter 2 of each specification, which states tag, nesting,
cardinality, value type and cross-reference target — everything an inventory
needs — as typeset text.

`scripts/spec55/transcribe.py` reads those chapters and writes the files 7.0
ships, under `testdata/spec/gedcom-5.5` and `testdata/spec/gedcom-5.5.1`.

Neither PDF is vendored, and neither is its prose. What is checked in is the
*facts* read out of them — tag, superstructure, cardinality, value type — plus
the individual grammar lines the defect table below has to quote to say what is
wrong with them. Each document states its own terms, and `SOURCE` records those
verbatim rather than paraphrasing:

| Version | Document | SHA-256 | Retrieved |
|---------|----------|---------|-----------|
| 5.5 | [`ged55.pdf`](https://gedcom.io/specifications/ged55.pdf) | `4949bd56a42d0a8c…` | 2026-08-18 |
| 5.5.1 | [`ged551.pdf`](https://gedcom.io/specifications/ged551.pdf) | `b81d16576ae8ad09…` | 2026-08-18 |

>
> **5.5.1** — Copyright © 1987, 1989, 1992, 1993, 1995, 1999 by The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.

A transcription is only as good as its proofreading, so
`scripts/spec55/crosscheck.py` checks it against two sources made without
reference to it: the 5.5 specification's own Appendix B, which lists every place
each substructure is spliced, and
[pjcj/Gedcom.pm](https://github.com/pjcj/Gedcom.pm)'s `.grammar` files, which are
someone else's transcription of the same chapters. Gedcom.pm is Perl-licensed
and nothing is copied from it; it is read and compared. The differences that
remain are listed in
[`testdata/spec/README.md`](../../testdata/spec/README.md), and each is a place
Gedcom.pm departs from the printed grammar where this follows it: mostly
structures it adds, two where it harmonizes an inconsistency 5.5.1 has with
itself, and one that is a difference in naming rather than in what the grammar
allows.

The files are test data. No library code reads them, and they add no runtime
dependency — this document is a report, not a parsing engine.

## How each status is derived

Identically to the 7.0 report, by `decoder/spec_common_test.go`, which both
harnesses share. For every pair it builds the smallest document of that version
containing the structure in that context, and the same document with that one
line removed. It decodes both and reads three signals:

- **the typed model** — the header, schema, detected vendor, and each record's
  parsed entity. If it differs between the two documents, the structure has
  typed access. Every `Tags` field is excluded from the comparison: that is the
  raw half of [ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-lossless-dual-storage.md)'s dual
  storage and holds every line regardless of support, so counting it would
  report everything as supported.
- **the diagnostics** — whether the decoder reported `UNKNOWN_TAG` for that line.
- **a sentinel tag** — `ZZZZ`, which no version of GEDCOM defines, placed in the
  same context. A context that reports the sentinel reports unknown tags at all;
  one that stays silent about the sentinel is silent about everything, so silence
  about a standard tag there says nothing. This separates `raw (accepted)` from
  `raw (undiagnosed)`, which are indistinguishable from the outside without it.

A `raw` status means there is no typed field for the structure, not that the
structure is dropped: every line is kept in `Record.Tags` under
[ADR 0003](../decisions/0003-lossless-dual-storage.md), whether the decoder
understands it or not. This report measures the decoder alone; the encoder,
validator and converter are not exercised here.

## Structure names

A 5.5.x structure is named for the grammar production that defines it and the
path of tags to it inside that production — `EVENT_DETAIL.DATE` is the `DATE`
line of `EVENT_DETAIL`. That is the same identity 7.0's URIs carry, spelled the
way these specifications name things: one structure stays one structure however
many places splice it in.

Two suffixes appear. A `#2` marks the second branch of an alternation that
reuses a tag — both specifications define `NOTE` twice in `NOTE_STRUCTURE`, once
as a pointer to a note record and once as inline text — and the two are
genuinely different structures that this library may support separately. A
production name inside the path, as in
`FAM_RECORD.FAM.FAMILY_EVENT_STRUCTURE.HUSB`, marks a line 5.5 writes beneath a
splice: `HUSB` there is a substructure of every family event tag, which is
exactly what 5.5.1 later named `FAMILY_EVENT_DETAIL`.

## What the numbers do not say

- **One context per structure, not every context.** A pair is measured at the
  shallowest place the grammar allows it. If this library handled a structure
  under one record and not another, only the measured one is reported.
- **The cardinality column is the grammar's, not a rule this library enforces.**
  It is recorded because the grammar states it. Nothing here validates against
  it; that is [ADR 0008](../decisions/0008-validator-architecture.md)'s territory
  and separate work.
- **A value the decoder would have chosen anyway is invisible.** The measurement
  is a difference between two decoded documents, so a line whose only typed
  effect is a value the model already holds cannot be seen. 5.5 is where this
  bites: the decoder falls back to 5.5 when a document states no version, so
  removing the version statement from a 5.5 document changes nothing, and
  `HEAD`, `HEAD.GEDC` and `HEAD.GEDC.VERS` read `raw (undiagnosed)` in 5.5 and
  `typed` in 5.5.1. The difference between those two columns is the fallback,
  not the decoder. `TestSpec55VersionFallbackIsInvisible` pins it so this note
  cannot quietly stop being true.
- **`typed` is not a claim of completeness.** It means the structure changed the
  typed model, not that every part of its payload was interpreted.
- **Every payload is invented.** The grammar names a value type; it does not
  supply an example. The harness synthesizes one. A decoder that accepted one
  plausible value and rejected another would be measured on the value it was
  given.
- **The drift test proves the report matches the decoder, not that the decoder is
  right.** A behaviour change fails it; a behaviour that was always wrong does
  not.

## What is being done about the gaps

Everything below that is not `typed` was triaged when this report was first
published, against the issues the 7.0 report had already raised. Most of it was
already tracked: attribute substructures reported as unknown ([#402]), event
detail dropping `RELI` ([#447]), family `CENS` and `RESI` never decoded
([#448]), and the header emitting no diagnostics at all ([#449]) between them
account for the bulk of the non-typed rows.

Two gaps were new, and neither could have come from the 7.0 half:

- **[#452]** — submission records reach no typed field at all. 7.0 removed
  `SUBN`, so only a 5.5.x inventory can show it.
- **[#453]** — 5.5.1's `FONE` and `ROMN` name variations are recognized and
  then dropped, where 7.0's equivalent `TRAN` is parsed into the typed model.

Read the table as a statement of where the library is, not as a backlog — the
backlog lives in the tracker.

[#402]: https://github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/issues/402
[#447]: https://github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/issues/447
[#448]: https://github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/issues/448
[#449]: https://github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/issues/449
[#452]: https://github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/issues/452
[#453]: https://github.com/cacack/gedcom-go/issues/453

## Regenerating

```bash
make spec-coverage
```

The document is checked in and compared on every test run, so a change in what
the decoder supports fails `TestSpec55Coverage` until it is regenerated. The
inventory itself is regenerated only by re-running the transcription against the
specification PDFs, which is described in
[`scripts/spec55/README.md`](../../scripts/spec55/README.md).

Places the printed grammar does not say what it means, and the reading
taken. Nothing here is corrected in the inventory — a transcription that
quietly repaired its source would be a different document than the one it
claims to describe.
